knownLimitations.summary: The commit field identifies the clean source commit tested before the manifest file is written.
knownLimitations.impact: A manifest committed later intentionally points to its tested parent/source commit and never claims to hash itself.

knownLimitations.summary: This local manifest records one host environment only.
knownLimitations.impact: It does not establish a supported operating-system or architecture matrix beyond separately linked CI evidence.

knownLimitations.summary: The existing ephemeral synthetic conversation remains an unaccepted preview.
knownLimitations.impact: R0 evidence cannot be used to claim the complete R1 coding-agent or terminal journey.

knownLimitations.summary: Evidence schema v1 records partial requirement progress only.
knownLimitations.impact: No requirement can be marked complete until a later schema binds implemented test identities to reviewed jobs and enforcement points.

knownLimitations.summary: Every R0 fixture and artifact hashed by the manifest is a tracked input at the tested commit.
knownLimitations.impact: Generated reports need a later provenance-bearing output descriptor rather than being treated as committed R0 input evidence.

knownLimitations.summary: R0 gate commands run in an isolated disposable checkout; macOS capture additionally denies source-tree reads and writes with inherited sandbox-exec policy, while non-macOS POSIX capture retains process-group/source-audit isolation. Schema v1 capture and replay fail closed on Windows until descendant process-tree containment exists.
knownLimitations.impact: The manifest records source isolation, not complete process-lifecycle containment. A descendant that creates a new session can escape the original process group and may briefly outlive capture; timeout handling closes retained pipes after a fixed grace so evidence fails instead of hanging, and the inherited macOS source denial still applies. Non-macOS POSIX capture assumes reviewed commands and locked dependencies are not actively malicious; stronger cross-platform process-tree isolation remains later work.

knownLimitations.summary: R0 bounds command wall time and each stdout/stderr stream, but does not impose OS-level CPU, memory, PID, disk, or ignored-output quotas.
knownLimitations.impact: Only reviewed locked gate commands are eligible for R0 capture. Host resource containment requires a future cgroup, container, job-object, or equivalent platform boundary and is not claimed by this manifest.

knownLimitations.summary: The 21 evidence-controller integration cases that launch nested captures are explicit skips when the repository suite is already running as an R0 evidence child because macOS sandbox-exec profiles cannot nest; five non-recursive controller cases still run.
knownLimitations.impact: Full controller integration coverage must pass in ordinary local and hosted CI outside self-capture. The R0 manifest attests its outer isolated commands and does not claim recursive self-attestation.

knownLimitations.summary: The local manifest contains no GitHub, pull-request, hosted-run, branch-protection, or merge identity.
knownLimitations.impact: R0 remains a candidate until those external records pass review and the candidate is merged to mainline.

knownLimitations.summary: R0 package smoke verifies the actual temporary tarball against a reviewed platform/architecture/npm-version gzip SHA-256/size, the cross-platform tar SHA-256/size, npm's SHA-1/SHA-512 metadata, and the exact 47-file type/mode/size/SHA-256 inventory before removing it.
knownLimitations.impact: The local R0 manifest retains reviewed macOS-arm64/npm-10, macOS-arm64/npm-11, and Linux-x64/npm-10 compression profiles plus the canonical tar digest through the hashed inventory, but not the distributable archive or a release signature; immutable artifact retention and provenance remain R10 work.

knownLimitations.summary: Command duration is retained as operational metadata and checked only against a bounded replay plausibility envelope.
knownLimitations.impact: R0 evidence attests exact command output bytes, digests, status, inputs, and environment, but it is not a performance benchmark or duration attestation; supported-platform percentile evidence remains R10 work.
